I first develop ten arguments in defense of AI-assisted writing, addressing objections ranging from its moral status and deskilling concerns to questions of attribution, disclosure, and cognitive biases. I then propose a framework drawing on an analogy to inquisitorial appellate courts, in which the academic author functions as an appellate judge who receives an initial output and must independently investigate, verify, and refine it before endorsing it as their own. Just as appellate systems rely on institutional safeguards-appointment criteria, rules of procedure, multi-tier review, and misconduct sanctions-to ensure legitimacy, the academic system can develop analogous mechanisms to govern responsible AI use. Drawing on the law and economics literature on judicial incentives, I develop a formal framework for aligning academic incentives with responsible AI deployment. The paper synthesizes these insights into a set of proposed best practices and concludes by discussing the limitations of the appellate court analogy.

AI.tldr: 本文为AI辅助学术写作辩护，提出在适当制度约束下，AI可以提升学术生产效率而不损害质量。作者首先提出十个支持AI写作的论点，然后借鉴上诉法院的类比框架，将学者比作上诉法官，需独立调查、验证和精炼AI输出。最后提出激励机制框架和最佳实践建议。
AI.research_question: 在适当的制度约束下，AI辅助学术写作如何能够既提高学术生产效率，又不损害学术质量？
AI.motivation: 生成式AI工具（如ChatGPT、Gemini、Claude）的快速普及引发了学术界关于AI辅助写作合法性的激烈辩论。批评者将其等同于作弊，担心幻觉、抄袭和学术标准侵蚀；支持者则认为AI能提高生产力，让研究者专注于实质性智力贡献。
AI.theoretical_framework: 1. 上诉法院类比框架：将学术作者比作上诉法官，需独立调查、验证和精炼AI初始输出；2. 法律与经济学文献中的司法激励机制；3. 制度约束理论：借鉴上诉系统的制度保障（任命标准、程序规则、多层审查、不当行为制裁）来规范AI使用。
AI.method: 1. 理论论证：提出十个支持AI辅助写作的论点，回应道德地位、技能退化、归属、披露和认知偏见等反对意见；2. 类比分析：建立上诉法院与学术系统的类比框架；3. 形式化框架：基于法律经济学文献，开发学术激励与负责任AI部署的正式框架。
AI.findings: 1. AI辅助学术写作在负责任实践和适当约束下是合理且有益的；2. 上诉法院类比提供了有效的制度框架来确保AI使用的合法性；3. 学术系统可以发展类似上诉系统的机制来管理AI使用；4. 需要将学术激励与负责任AI部署相结合。
AI.theory_contributions: 1. 为AI辅助学术写作提供了系统的理论辩护；2. 提出了创新的上诉法院类比框架；3. 开发了基于法律经济学的正式激励框架；4. 拓展了学术诚信和AI伦理的理论边界。
AI.practical_contributions: 1. 提出了一套AI辅助学术写作的最佳实践建议；2. 为学术机构制定AI使用政策提供了制度设计参考；3. 为学者如何负责任地使用AI提供了具体指导；4. 讨论了上诉法院类比的局限性，为实践应用提供警示。

title: Default-triggered Acquisition (IV): The American Option-to-Acquire
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Default-triggered Acquisition (IV): The American Option-to-Acquire

declarations.funderStatement: The author was supported by a PhD scholarship from the Cambridge Overseas Trust.

detail.abstract: Cheung and Satchell (2004) and Cheung (2004a) address the default-triggered acquisition (DTA) issue, and derives some analytical results for risky bond pricing based on the assumption that acquisitions only take place in the instance of a default. This paper aims to examine the viability of this assumption. Rather than modelling from the bond investors' point of view, Cheung (2004b) analyses the DTA problem from the potential acquirers' perspective, and develops a structural model of a potential acquirer's position, i.e. the European option-to-acquire, with analytical results. This paper considers pre-default acquisition opportunities, and extends its argument into an exploration of the corresponding American option-to-acquire. Numerical results are derived for a comprehensive numerical comparative static analysis. The comparison of the European and American positions allows some insight into the circumstances in which DTAs are important. Abstract Addendum (2026): This paper provides the definitive link between credit risk and the optimal timing of M&A. By extending the framework to include the American option-to-acquire, it captures the strategic value of 'pre-default' interventions. This is particularly relevant in today's private credit and distressed debt markets, where the decision to trigger a restructuring or acquisition before a formal default is a critical driver of internal rate of return for institutional investors.

AI.tldr: 本文检验了违约触发收购(DTA)假设的可行性，将分析从欧洲式收购期权扩展到美式收购期权，探讨了违约前收购机会的重要性，并建立了信用风险与并购最优时机之间的联系。
AI.research_question: 违约触发收购(DTA)假设是否可行？在什么情况下违约前收购机会对潜在收购者具有重要价值？
AI.motivation: 先前研究(Cheung and Satchell, 2004; Cheung, 2004a)假设收购仅在违约发生时进行，本文旨在检验这一假设的合理性，并考虑违约前收购机会的重要性。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于期权定价理论的结构模型，将潜在收购者的决策建模为欧洲式期权(仅在违约时执行)和美式期权(可在违约前任何时间执行)的收购选择权。
AI.method: 开发潜在收购者位置的结构模型，进行全面的数值比较静态分析，比较欧洲式和美式收购期权的价值差异。
AI.findings: 数值分析结果表明，在某些情况下违约前收购机会具有重要价值，美式期权比欧洲式期权提供更大的灵活性，特别是在私人信贷和困境债务市场中。
AI.theory_contributions: 建立了信用风险与并购最优时机之间的理论联系，扩展了违约触发收购框架，将违约前干预的战略价值纳入分析。
AI.practical_contributions: 为机构投资者在私人信贷和困境债务市场中的决策提供指导，特别是在决定是否在正式违约前触发重组或收购时，这对内部收益率是关键驱动因素。

title: Platform Competition Through Composition: Engagement Heterogeneity, Data Accumulation, and Market Tipping

detail.title: Platform Competition Through Composition: Engagement Heterogeneity, Data Accumulation, and Market Tipping
detail.abstract: Why do smaller platforms sometimes overtake larger rivals? This paper studies one mechanism through which user composition can matter as much as user count. Conditional on an early sorting advantage among high-engagement producers, platforms serving those users accumulate data faster, improve quality sooner, and may cross a tipping threshold that leads to dominance. Three results follow. First, the dominance condition links design quality and the engagement premium to the tipping threshold: conditional on Phase~0 producer sorting, the platform whose design-composition product exceeds its rival's wins from any equal or better starting position. Second, greater engagement heterogeneity lowers the tipping threshold and implies a cross-market association between contribution inequality and concentration. Third, concentration has distributional welfare effects: producers benefit from quality improvements while consumers bear mismatch costs. The model therefore suggests caution with uniform policy thresholds and points toward engagement-contingent interventions as a possible design principle.

AI.tldr: 该研究探讨了小型平台如何超越大型竞争对手的机制，指出用户构成（特别是高参与度生产者的早期排序优势）比用户数量更重要。平台通过积累数据、提升质量，可能跨越临界点实现主导地位。
AI.research_question: 为什么小型平台有时能超越大型竞争对手？用户构成如何影响平台竞争结果？
AI.motivation: 理解平台竞争中除了用户数量之外的其他关键因素，特别是用户构成（尤其是高参与度生产者）如何影响平台发展轨迹和最终市场结构。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于网络效应、用户参与度异质性、数据积累和质量改进的平台竞争理论框架，强调"设计-构成乘积"和"临界点阈值"概念。
AI.method: 理论建模方法，分析平台竞争动态，推导主导条件、临界点阈值和福利效应。
AI.findings: 1. 平台主导条件取决于设计质量与参与度溢价的乘积；2. 参与度异质性降低临界点阈值，导致贡献不平等与市场集中度关联；3. 集中度产生分配福利效应：生产者受益于质量改进，消费者承担匹配成本。
AI.theory_contributions: 1. 提出用户构成作为平台竞争的关键机制；2. 建立"设计-构成乘积"决定平台主导的理论框架；3. 揭示参与度异质性与市场集中度的理论联系。
AI.practical_contributions: 1. 建议政策制定者避免统一阈值；2. 提出基于参与度的干预措施作为设计原则；3. 为平台管理者提供用户构成管理策略。

title: AV-MapNet: A Vascular Topology-Guided Network for PreciseRetinal Vessel Segmentation and Artery–Vein Classification
affiliations: Queensland University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Queensland University of Technology

detail.title: AV-MapNet: A Vascular Topology-Guided Network for PreciseRetinal Vessel Segmentation and Artery–Vein Classification
detail.abstract: Accurate retinal vessel segmentation and artery–vein (AV) classification are essential for computer-aided diagnosis of cardiovascular and ophthalmic diseases, yet most existing methods treat these tasks separately and rely on heuristic post-processing, limiting robustness in complex vascular structures and pathological conditions. In this work, we propose AV-MapNet, a topology-aware and computationally efficient sequential deep learning framework that jointly performs vessel segmentation and AV classification in an end-to-end manner. The architecture incorporates lightweight mini encoder–decoder refinement modules as learned structural regularizers to enforce vascular continuity and topological consistency, while dilated convolutions, multi-scale feature extraction, and Gaussian-weighted refinement enhance sensitivity to thin vessels and preserve anatomical details. Extensive experiments on multiple public retinal datasets demonstrate that AV-MapNet achieves state-of-the-art performance, with segmentation accuracies of 98.3%, 98.6%, and 98.5% on RITE, DRIVE, and HRF datasets, respectively, and Dice scores of 87.01%, 88.20%, and 87.60%. For AV classification, the model achieves accuracies of 95.2% on LES-AV, 96.6% on AV-DRIVE, and 97.0% on RITE, with consistently high Dice scores and strong precision, sensitivity, and specificity. These results confirm the robustness of the proposed framework in handling pathological variability and complex vessel crossings, while maintaining low computational complexity, making AV-MapNet suitable for real-time clinical and teleophthalmology applications.

title: AI-Driven Alpha Decay: Algorithmic Homogenization, Reflexive Signal Erosion, and the Paradox of Intelligent Markets
affiliations: and

detail.title: AI-Driven Alpha Decay: Algorithmic Homogenization, Reflexive Signal Erosion, and the Paradox of Intelligent Markets
detail.abstract: We show that AI-driven investment strategies are inherently self-defeating at scale. As AI adoption rises, three mutually reinforcing channels-signal crowding, performative signal erosion, and Red Queen competition-compress excess returns. We derive the alpha half-life h(ϕ) = ln 2/[θ + δ(ϕ)], where θ is the natural mean-reversion rate and δ(ϕ) = N ϕρa/λ(ϕ) is the AI-accelerated decay component, which is convex-decreasing in adoption. At current adoption levels (ϕ ≈ 0.7, ρ ≈ 0.6), the model implies signal half-lives of 18 months versus 5-7 years pre-AI. We establish four theoretical results. First, the alpha half-life theorem: signal lifespans are convex-decreasing in AI adoption. Second, a signal extinction cascade: beyond a critical threshold ϕ * , the decay of one signal class triggers accelerated competition for remaining signals. Third, a Red Queen impossibility: in the monoculture equilibrium, net alpha is identically zero despite heavy AI investment. Fourth, a fragility-efficiency.

title: When AI Levels the Playing Field: Skill Homogenization, Asset Concentration, and Two Regimes of Inequality
affiliations: and

detail.title: When AI Levels the Playing Field: Skill Homogenization, Asset Concentration, and Two Regimes of Inequality
detail.abstract: Generative AI compresses within-task skill differences while shifting economic value toward concentrated complementary assets, creating an apparent paradox: the technology that equalizes individual performance may widen aggregate inequality. We formalize this tension in a task-based model with endogenous education, employer screening, and heterogeneous firms. The model yields two regimes whose boundary depends on AI's technology structure (proprietary vs. commodity) and labor market institutions (rent-sharing elasticity, asset concentration). A scenario analysis via Method of Simulated Moments, matching six empirical targets, disciplines the model's quantitative magnitudes; a sensitivity decomposition reveals that the five non-∆Gini moments identify mechanism rates but not the aggregate sign, which at the calibrated parameters is pinned by m 6 and ξ, while AI's technology structure (η 1 vs. η 0) independently crosses the boundary. The contribution is the mechanismnot a verdict on the sign. Occupation-level regressions using BLS OEWS data (2019-2023) illustrate why such data cannot test the model's task-level predictions. The predictions are testable with within-occupation, within-task panel data that do not yet exist at scale.

title: Macroeconomic Approach of the Pandemic COVID -19
affiliations: International Balkan University, International Balkan University, University of Tetovo and Independent

detail.title: Macroeconomic Approach of the Pandemic COVID -19

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Public data used.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract: The pandemic COVID-19 represents not only a global health crises, but also a global finical crises, coming up with human and economic costs that tend to be higher at developing countries, due to their health care system, informal economic sector lower fiscal space, corruption, etc. Although each country have taken its individual measures regarding the pandemic COVID-19, it is needed an international coordination in the economic policy, health care and science to face with its consequences. In this regard, the main objective of this paper is to highlight the importance of the economic measures that governments around the world have taken in response to the Covid-19 pandemic which can vary in length and scope, to review the recent papers regarding the macro effects of the pandemic COVID-19 as well as to emphasize the COVID-19 Economic Stimulus Index (CESI) that contains fiscal, monetary, and exchange rate measures, created by Elgin et al. (2020), based on the data for 166 rich, middle and low income countries. In addition, in this paper are only taken into consideration the fiscal and monetary stimulus. The results imply that richer countries have a larger economic stimulus package and adopt a larger fiscal and monetary stimulus.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Systemic Risk: A Unified Model of Performative Prediction, Algorithmic Herding, and Cognitive Dependency in Financial Markets

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and Systemic Risk: A Unified Model of Performative Prediction, Algorithmic Herding, and Cognitive Dependency in Financial Markets
detail.abstract: We develop a unified model in which AI adoption in financial markets generates systemic risk through three mutually reinforcing channels: performative prediction, algorithmic herding, and cognitive dependency. Within an extended rational expectations framework with endogenous adoption, we derive an equilibrium systemic risk coupling r(ϕ) = ϕρβ/λ ′ (ϕ), where ϕ is the AI adoption share, ρ the algorithmic signal correlation, β the performative feedback intensity, and λ ′ (ϕ) the endogenous effective price impact. Because λ ′ (ϕ) is decreasing in ϕ, the coupling is convex in adoption, implying that the systemic risk multiplier M = (1-r)-1 grows superlinearly as AI penetration increases. title: Green Public Procurement under Natural Disasters: Evidence from Earthquakes in Japan
affiliations: Avignon University

detail.title: Green Public Procurement under Natural Disasters: Evidence from Earthquakes in Japan
detail.abstract: Public procurement is increasingly used as a public policy instrument, particularly to achieve environmental objectives. Since green public procurement stimulates innovation and fosters sustainable production processes, it is crucial to assess its sensitivity to natural disasters. To our knowledge, this paper is the first to study this question. Original data on municipal procurement in Japan are combined with city-level seismic data between 2012 and 2020 in a difference-in-differences design. We find robust evidence of a negative impact of earthquakes on municipal green public procurement, particularly in sectors where sustainable practices are less prevalent. The results also indicate a negative impact of post-disaster repair expenditures, instrumented using original data on municipal bridges and tunnels, on the implementation of green procurement practices. Given the increasing frequency and intensity of natural disasters, these findings highlight how natural hazards can force a trade-off between reconstruction needs and local environmental governance.

title: Taxing and nudging to reduce carbon emissions
affiliations: University of Toulouse Capitole - Toulouse School of Economics, Swedish National Road and Transport Research Institute, University of Toulouse Capitole - Toulouse School of Economics, affiliation not provided to SSRN, French National Institute for Agricultural Research (INRA) - Grenoble Applied Economic Laboratory, University of Newcastle and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Taxing and nudging to reduce carbon emissions
detail.abstract: What can be done to reduce the carbon footprint of consumption? To answer this, we conducted an online shopping experiment that tested the effects of two policy tools: a carbon tax (at two levels) and a color-coded carbon label. To disentangle the tax's substitution effect from its income effect, we held consumers' purchasing power constant. We find that the tax alone significantly reduces the carbon footprint per euro spent but not per basket purchased, implying that the reduction is driven purely by the income effect. The label alone makes consumers buy fewer red products and more green products, although without reducing significantly their carbon footprint. We find a significant reduction of the carbon footprint per basket only when the tax is high enough and combined with the label. Next, we perform a welfare analysis grounded on a theoretical framework that accommodates for several assumptions about consumer's preferences and motivations. We estimate the loss of consumer's surplus from nudging consumers with the label. We also estimate the consumers' valuation of a ton of CO2 avoided when they care about their climate impact.

The Architecture of Systemic Failure in Argentine Anesthetic Control

detail.abstract: Two distinct events — separated by institutional level and causal mechanism yet converging in structural outcome — expose a shared vulnerability in Argentina's management of critical anesthetic substances. In February 2026, anesthesiologist Alejandro Zalazar was found dead from a propofol and fentanyl overdose. Tracing the confiscated compounds led to the Hospital Italiano de Buenos Aires, initiating judicial proceedings (Case File No. 8922/2026) against two members of its anesthesiology department, accused of operating a diversion circuit from 2023 through mid-February 2026. Eight months earlier, in May 2025, the Hospital Italiano de La Plata identified a cluster of multidrug-resistant bacteremia among hospitalized patients. The source was traced to fentanyl ampoules produced by HLB Pharma Group S.A. and manufactured at Laboratorios Ramallo S.A., contaminated with Klebsiella pneumoniae and Ralstonia pickettii. That event resulted in at least 111 confirmed deaths (Case File FLP 17371/2025), constituting the largest recorded pharmaceutical public health disaster in Argentina. These cases are not independent anomalies. They instantiate the same structural condition: a control architecture in which access and oversight are effectively co-located, verification operates retrospectively rather than in real time, and detection depends on harm reaching a threshold sufficient to trigger external intervention. The failure modes differ — internal diversion versus industrial contamination — but the upstream deficit is singular: no layer of the system identified a sustained, lethal process before a third party forced its visibility.

title: How spatial spillovers affect the performance of action- and result-based conservation payments
affiliations: Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research - UFZ (Leipzig)

detail.title: How spatial spillovers affect the performance of action- and result-based conservation payments
detail.abstract: Biodiversity conservation policy in agricultural landscapes largely relies on payments that offset the profit losses that are associated with biodiversity-friendly land-use measures. Action-based payments reward the conservation measures directly, while the increasingly promoted result-based payments reward the ecological outcomes of conservation efforts. Result-based payments have been shown theoretically and empirically to be efficient when conservation costs are spatially heterogeneous. Often mentioned as an open issue but not yet addressed in this context is the role of ecological spillover, so that conservation efforts one one farm affect the effectiveness of conservation efforts on other farms. Using a stylised model of two farms, I show that negative spillover (that may arise from the concave species area relationship present in most ecosystems) favours action-based payments and disfavours result-based payments, while positive spillover (that may arise from landscape-scale population dynamics observed in species that are structured as metapopulations) favours both payments but particularly the result-based payment. The effect of asymmetry in the spillover depends on whether the spillover is positive or negative and on how the spillover asymmetry relates to the heterogeneity in the conservation costs.

title: International Sanctions and Corruption
affiliations: University of Hamburg - Institute of Law and Economics, University of Trier - Faculty of Economics and University of Trier - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: International Sanctions and Corruption

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: A major concern about the imposition of international sanctions is that they may permanently deteriorate the quality of institutions in target countries, potentially causing an increase in corruption. While case studies suggest that this is frequently the case, systematic evidence is so far missing. We provide the first cross-country statistical analysis of the impact of sanctions on public-sector corruption. Using a panel difference-in-differences model and an event study approach, we analyze sanctions against 125 countries from 1971 to 2019. Our results show that Western (and UN) sanctions cause a significant decline of corruption in democracies, while non-Western sanctions and those targeting autocracies have no systematic impact. Event study estimates time the reductions in corruption at about three to four years into the sanctions episode. They persist throughout the sanctions period, but once sanctions are lifted, corruption levels revert to their pre-treatment baseline, indicating that the corruption-reducing effect is limited to the duration of the sanctions episode. Further analysis reveals that the effect is stronger when sanctions explicitly target democratization or human rights improvements.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces DREFS-a five-module gap-analysis codification built on the Behaviour Change Intervention Ontology (BCIO) and applied in the AISA 11.1 bot system. DREFS stands for Dose, Reach, Engagement, Fidelity, and Schedule-the five most common structural dimensions of intervention non-achievement, independent of whether the intervention content was theoretically appropriate. The codification comprises 260 module-level entries across five modules drawn from 224 unique ontology IDs. The five BCIO sub-ontology modules corresponding to these dimensions are currently marked as Coming Soon on bciosearch.org. DREFS provides an interim ontology-backed vocabulary for these dimensions. Every entry carries a verified identifier from BCIO, MeSH, GO, MF, MFOEM, ADDICTO, PDRO, APA, or iSci-no free labels. Entries carry one of three status codes: CROSS (existing BCIO-ecosystem term assigned a DREFS module suffix), IMPORT-BCIO (term officially imported into BCIO from an external ontology), and IMPORT-AUTHOR (term imported by the author from an external ontology, assigned to BCIO modules in bcio_index, filling a conceptual gap where neither BCIO nor officially BCIOimported ontologies provided a suitable identifier; no ontological hierarchy established; level assigned by author on semantic grounds). There are 209 CROSS entries, 22 IMPORT-BCIO entries, and 29 IMPORT-AUTHOR entries. 31 IDs appear in two or more modules simultaneously-each module appearance carries a distinct causal rationale. All 260 entries are presented with full ontology IDs including module-position suffixes, ontology definitions, and module-specific rationale.

title: Introduction:High Rates and Low Taxes:  Tax Dodging in Mid-Century America (Cambridge University Press 2026)
affiliations: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - School of Law

detail.title: Introduction:High Rates and Low Taxes:  Tax Dodging in Mid-Century America (Cambridge University Press 2026)

publicationDetails.detailsText: Introduction: High Rates and Low Taxes: Tax Dodging in Mid-Century America (Cambridge University Press 2026); UCLA School of Law, Law-Econ Research Paper No. 26-02
publicationDetails.journalName: University of California, Los Angeles School of Law, Law & Economics Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Amidst calls for a return to the high tax rates of the 1950s and 60s, this is the introduction to a book that examines the tax dodging that accompanied it. Rather than being a period where, as Emmanuel Saez and Gabriel Zucman wrote, “tax dodging was kept in check,” this was the golden age of tax dodging in the United States, when it was brazenly public, sometimes outlandish, and often explicitly or implicitly condoned by politicians. 

This book fills a gap in the literature by focusing not just on the tax dodging of the top 1 percent, but on tax dodging’s spread throughout all income classes.  Lacking the political will to lower the top rates, Congress riddled the laws with loopholes, exemptions, and preferences, while largely accepting income tax chiseling’s rise in American culture. The rich and famous openly invested in tax shelters and de-camped to exotic tax havens, executives revamped the compensation and retirement schemes of their corporations to suit their tax needs, and an industry of tax advisers developed to help the general public engage in their own form of tax dodging through exaggerated expense accounts, luxurious business travel, and self-help books on “how the insider’s get rich on tax-wise” investments.  Tax dodging was a part of almost every restaurant bill, feature film, and savings account. It was literally woven into the fabric of society. 

This is not to say that mid-century tax dodging is an argument against high progressive rates.  Instead, it is a lesson in the risks of implicit tax cuts.  High rates accompanied by plentiful escape hatches only emboldened those who took advantage of them and disheartened those left out, leaving them feeling entitled to identify their own do-it-yourself tax dodging opportunities.  It was the backtracking from the high rates, particularly in a non-transparent way for the benefit primarily of the rich and famous, that made tax dodging a social and cultural phenomenon in mid-century America.

title: The 'Z-Score' of Vision 2030: Predicting Corporate Insolvency in the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul) Using Machine Learning
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The 'Z-Score' of Vision 2030: Predicting Corporate Insolvency in the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul) Using Machine Learning
detail.abstract: This research evaluates the applicability of Western bankruptcy models to the Saudi Arabian market and develops a localized machine learning model (the 'KSA-Score') to predict corporate distress. Addressing critical methodological flaws in prior literature, this study utilizes an exogenous distress label based on real regulatory events (e.g., Financial Restructuring Procedure filings, Capital Market Authority suspensions) to eliminate target leakage. The dataset comprises 364 firm-year observations from 91 non financial companies listed on the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul) between 2021 and 2025, integrating forensic accounting ratios with macroeconomic variables (Brent crude, non-oil GDP growth, SAIBOR). Utilizing Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and stratified 10-fold cross-validation, the analysis demonstrates that the traditional Altman Z-Score performs poorly in the Saudi context (Accuracy = 62.2%, F1 = 0.308). In contrast, ensemble machine learning models, particularly Gradient Boosting, achieve superior predictive power (Accuracy = 91.0%, AUC = 0.916). Threshold optimization using an asymmetric cost function (Type II error = 5x Type I error) further refines practical applicability. Logistic regression coefficients with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals reveal that retained earnings to total assets is the only statistically significant predictor (p < .001) of exogenous distress, highlighting the unique capital structures of Saudi corporations under Vision 2030.

title: Prediction Market Accuracy: Crowd Wisdom or Informed Minority?
affiliations: London Business School, , Yale University and London Business School

detail.title: Prediction Market Accuracy: Crowd Wisdom or Informed Minority?
detail.abstract: Prediction markets are remarkably accurate, yet the source of this accuracy remains poorly understood. The conventional view attributes it to crowd wisdom, whereby prices aggregate information from a large and diverse pool of participants. We show instead that accuracy is driven by a small minority of informed traders. Using the universe of transactions from a large prediction market platform, we identify these traders and show that they, around 3% of all accounts, generate the bulk of price discovery. Their trades predict future prices and final outcomes, make prices more accurate throughout a market's lifespan, and react to news the moment it arrives. The remaining majority does not produce accuracy; rather, it funds it. Their trades generate most of the volume, but little of the information, and their losses flow as profits to the informed minority. Prediction market accuracy thus reflects the wisdom of an informed minority, not the wisdom of the crowd.

title: Sample Composition Fragility in Demographic-Macro Research: A Diagnostic Framework

detail.title: Sample Composition Fragility in Demographic-Macro Research: A Diagnostic Framework
detail.abstract: Demographic variables are widely used in crosscountry panel regressions to explain capital flows, interest rates, exchange rate regimes, and fiscal dynamics. Yet the literature reports strikingly contradictory findings: demographic effects on the current account are positive in some studies, negative in others, and null in several OECD-focused panels. We show that these contradictions are the expected consequence of a multi-dimensional coefficient surface. Using a 141-country panel covering 97% of world population and 99% of world GDP, we estimate demographic effects across 18 papers and 45 major findings, classifying results as robust (20 findings, 44%), conditional (16 findings, 36%), or spurious (9 findings, 20%). The coefficient on the leading demographic variable (Z₁) ranges from-112 to +98 on the current account alone, depending on a country's income level, institutional configuration, and monetary regime. A pooled linear estimate averages over this surface, and the result depends entirely on which countries are in the sample. We identify four mechanisms that determine where on the surface a given sample sits-OECD composition weight, GDP/capita confounding, influential observation clusters, and the KAOPEN-income confound-and propose a nine-item diagnostic toolkit for researchers working with demographic variables in crosscountry panels.

title: Shield and Blindfold: Agentic AI, Anonymity, and the Civil Rights Inversion
affiliations: Avyayam Holdings and Singapore Management University - Lee Kong Chian School of Business

detail.title: Shield and Blindfold: Agentic AI, Anonymity, and the Civil Rights Inversion
detail.abstract: AI agents can transact with retailers and platforms on behalf of a human principal without revealing whom they represent, returning to commerce a degree of anonymity that has not been practically available since cash. The civil rights implications run in both directions. The architecture of discrimination collapses when the buyer is a shell-a retailer that cannot identify its counterparty cannot proxy-discriminate. But the same collapse defeats the evidentiary infrastructure on which civil rights enforcement relies. Disparate-treatment doctrine needs comparators. Disparate impact doctrine needs a protected class within the defendant's customer base. Iqbal-era pleading rigor needs facts the anonymity regime prevents from existing. The mechanism that forecloses discrimination also forecloses its proof. This Article argues that the resulting civil rights inversion requires the law to decide whether agent-mediated anonymity should be treated as civil rights infrastructure, how abuse can be regulated without forcing reidentification, and whether retailers may refuse to deal with agents at all.

title: Towards sustainable tropical pasture-based cattle fattening systems: insights from animal performance, methane emissions, and integrated environmental indices
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of São Paulo (USP) - Faculty of Veterinary Medicine and Animal Science, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Embrapa Southeast Livestock, Embrapa Southeast Livestock, Embrapa Pecuaria Sudeste, Embrapa Southeast Livestock, Embrapa Southeast Livestock, University of São Paulo (USP) - Center of Nuclear Energy in Agriculture (CENA), Embrapa Southeast Livestock and University of São Paulo (USP)

detail.title: Towards sustainable tropical pasture-based cattle fattening systems: insights from animal performance, methane emissions, and integrated environmental indices
detail.abstract: Sustainable intensification of pasture-based livestock systems is essential to increase beef production while mitigating environmental impacts, particularly enteric methane (CH4) emissions. Thus, we aimed to study the intensification of pasture-based systems in a multidisciplinary and innovative manner, evaluating effects on forage characteristics, animal performance, enteric emissions, and developing integrated environmental indicators. This study evaluated three systems during the rainy and dry seasons: degraded pasture (DEG), nitrogen-fertilized recovered pasture (REC), and an intercropped system with pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan) and Urochloa spp. (MIX), with three replicates per treatment (n =18). Thirty-six finishing Nellore cattle were used. Forage samples were collected by hand-plucking and chemically analyzed, while fecal stable isotope analysis was applied to estimate the botanical composition of ingested dry matter (C4 vs. C3 plants). Higher nutrient availability was observed in the MIX and REC systems. Although dry matter intake and CH4 emissions per animal did not differ among treatments, the MIX system supported higher stocking rates, a greater land-saving effect, and lower CH4 emissions per animal unit. The dry season associated with reduced diet quality and increased CH4 emission intensity. The Environmental Impact Scores (EISGB) —Environmental Impact Score for Beef Cattle Grazing Systems and Environmental Impact Score for Dry Matter Intake (EISDMI)—indicated greater eco-efficiency of the MIX and REC systems during the rainy season and highlighted the vulnerability of DEG pastures across seasons. Overall, integrating pigeon pea into tropical pastures improved productivity, nutrient supply, and environmental performance, demonstrating its potential as a sustainable strategy for beef production.

title: Closing the Integrity Gap: Information Integrity on Climate Change in the Construction Sector

detail.title: Closing the Integrity Gap: Information Integrity on Climate Change in the Construction Sector

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no conflicts of interest to this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not contain any studies with human or animal subjects performed by any of the authors.
declarations.funderStatement: The research is funded by Coteccons Construction Joint Stock Company, Vietnam.

detail.abstract: The construction sector is central to global decarbonisation, yet its climate trajectory is increasingly shaped not only by engineering and finance but by the quality of information that circulates within and around it. This paper argues that information integrity on climate change-the accuracy, completeness, transparency, and accountability of climate-related information-is now a core condition for credible climate action in construction rather than a peripheral communications concern. We ask: How does information integrity (or its absence) influence climate-related decisions, risks, and outcomes in the construction sector, and what governance framework is needed to address this? Methodologically, the paper synthesises emerging global policy developments (notably COP30's Declaration on Information Integrity and the Global Initiative for Information Integrity on Climate Change), literature on misinformation, greenwashing and ESG reporting, and recent reviews on sociotechnical barriers to decarbonising the built environment. It integrates these with practitioner reflections and an indicative case from Viet Nam's Coteccons to develop a four-pillar framework for "integrity-first" climate information in construction: data, reporting, communication, and governance. The paper offers a contrarian critique of current ESG and net-zero practices and proposes concrete steps for regulators, firms, and standard-setters. It aims to reposition information integrity as climate infrastructure for the construction sector.

title: Who Gets to Be Biased? How AI Supply Chains Over-Represent the West and Marginalize the Rest
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business and

detail.title: Who Gets to Be Biased? How AI Supply Chains Over-Represent the West and Marginalize the Rest
detail.abstract:
Efforts to mitigate AI bias have intensified, yet a deeper epistemic asymmetry remains overlooked by most: before a bias can be scrutinized, it must first be deemed worthy of inclusion in the first place.

The biases most discussed and scrutinized in AI today are primarily shaped by the geopolitical and infrastructural dominance of three major AI ecosystems: OpenAI, Anthropic, and DeepSeek. Developed within specific regulatory, cultural, and economic frameworks, these models extend beyond embodiment of ethics, biases and norms. They operationalize cultural power through AI’s supply chain. The infrastructures of dataset collection, model training, and computational access overwhelmingly privilege dominant geopolitical actors, ensuring that AI becomes not just a technological tool but an instrument of cultural and epistemic hegemony, establishing and reinforcing digital inequalities at a systemic level.

Each of these ecosystems possess their own approach to content moderation, discrimination, and censorship, spurring considerable academic discourse. Yet, this growing body of work has neglected to examine a fundamental question: what about the biases that never make it into the system at all?

What AI does not learn is as revealing as what it does. Entire worldviews, linguistic structures, and moral frameworks are deemed unfit for algorithmic inclusion, whether due to economic neglect, linguistic complexity, or their mere incompatibility with dominant AI-producing infrastructures. This is not accidental; it is the direct result of a newly emerging techno-colonial hierarchy where the most computationally expedient and economically dominant perspectives dictate the epistemic terrain, leaving the rest unheard, unmodeled, and computationally irrelevant.

Given the current setup of AI supply chains, perspectives from underrepresented cultural or linguistic communities risk erasure, with practical implications for how AI-assisted decisions unfold in healthcare, local governance, and digital economies. Moreover, our collective thinking, now heavily reliant on AI models, gravitates toward certain normative positions, neglecting valuable alternative insights or ethical priorities in a manner undergirds a novel form of techno-colonialism.

While classic colonial frameworks involved direct territorial control, today’s softer power is exerted through intangible digital infrastructures, data pipelines, and algorithmic preferences. The effects of a subtle hegemonic “cultural AI norming” are entirely invisible; hidden in the embeddings as AI models trained on predominantly Western or large-state datasets inject non-local biases into regions with entirely different historical and cultural contexts.

By continuing to build global AI on a non-global supply chain without addressing these privileges, we will risk adopting AI models that will accelerate a digital-era colonial project, in which certain worldviews dominate while others go unacknowledged. This risk compels us to address a deeper, structural question: how do we ensure that the full spectrum of human perspectives—biases included—become accessible for discussion rather than excluded from consideration altogether?

title: Beyond `Degrowth': Communicating Sustainability via Ethical Security Economics, Occupational Security, and Release from Materialist Trauma Bonds
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond `Degrowth': Communicating Sustainability via Ethical Security Economics, Occupational Security, and Release from Materialist Trauma Bonds
detail.abstract: Degrowth scholarship presents a compelling ecological imperative but faces persistent public communication challenges rooted in the term's perceived negativity, its association with economic recession, and its systematic political marginalization. This paper argues that these communication failures reflect a deeper structural dynamic: publics have developed pathological attachments to growth-based political-economic systems through cycles of policy promise and betrayal that closely resemble trauma bonding in interpersonal contexts. These bonds are maintained and deliberately deepened through materialist and consumerist ideologies that reduce human identity to market participation, sever communities from ecological and spiritual meaning, and position capital flows as the primary medium through which politicians sustain loyalty despite chronic governance failure. Communicating degrowth effectively therefore requires not only a positive reorientation of its framing but a theoretically grounded account of why materialist ontologies, which dominate conventional economics and most post-growth frameworks alike, are structurally incapable of releasing people from these bonds. We propose ethical security economics (ESE) {redacted} as an integrative communication framework grounded in occupational security theory {redacted} and its five core values of sustainability, justice, peace, compassion, and authenticity with accuracy. Drawing on the Socio-Political-Ecological-Community (SPEC) framework {redacted}, we argue that its explicit grounding in spiritual ontology, the insistence that life possesses intrinsic sacred worth preceding all material valuation, represents a contribution that no existing materialist framework can replicate. This spiritual dimension is not supplementary but central: it is precisely what materialist political economy suppresses, and its recovery is the most powerful mechanism for dissolving the trauma bonds that extractive systems engineer and exploit. Seven concrete communication principles are developed for policy, civil society, and academic engagement, with application demonstrated through systematic ESE analysis of Canadian energy governance failures, charting a path toward transformative public discourse grounded in values that capital cannot manufacture.

title: The Convergence Cascade: Why the Collision of Artificial Intelligence and Systemic Financial Fragility Creates an Irreversible Economic Reckoning

detail.title: The Convergence Cascade: Why the Collision of Artificial Intelligence and Systemic Financial Fragility Creates an Irreversible Economic Reckoning

detail.abstract: This paper presents a unified thesis for why the global economy, and specifically the United States, is approaching a systemic disruption of a scale and character that has no historical precedent. Unlike previous economic crises, which had identifiable causes, containable damage, and recoverable trajectories, the convergence described here is selfreinforcing, accelerating, and structurally irreversible. The core systemic risk is not AI capability alone. It is the interaction between autonomy-at-scale, capital concentration, regulatory lag, and leveraged financial structures. If displacement accelerates faster than redistribution and enforcement mechanisms can adapt, systemic instability becomes not merely possible but mathematically overdetermined. The thesis rests on five interlocking pillars: the crossing of a qualitative threshold in artificial intelligence capability, now measurable in real deployments rather than projections; the geopolitical arms race dynamic that makes deceleration structurally impossible; a financial system already stretched beyond every historical stress limit simultaneously; a top-down displacement mechanism that attacks the load-bearing columns of consumer spending rather than the base; and a government response toolkit that is not designed for structural transformation and will, in attempting to respond, accelerate the wealth concentration dynamics that make the crisis severe. The central argument is not that something will go wrong. It is that the mechanisms required for things to go right no longer exist. The window in which preparation is possible is open, but it will not remain open indefinitely.

title: Does automation decrease fertility? A new channel
affiliations: Universidade de Coimbra and Universidade de Coimbra

detail.title: Does automation decrease fertility? A new channel
detail.abstract: This paper develops a dynamic task-based general equilibrium model to study how automation affects fertility through wages, job displacement, and the price of child services. Households differ by task type (innate ability, learned, and reskilling) and choose consumption, fertility, and time devoted to childrearing under endogenous wage dynamics. On the production side, a task allocation framework with automation determines wage schedules, skill thresholds, and displacement risk. Automation raises the productivity of robotic capital, shifts task boundaries, and increases educational requirements, generating heterogeneous income paths and reskilling incentives. We show that fertility responds to both direct and opportunity costs of children, with the sign of wage growth effects depending on the elasticity of substitution between fertility and parental time. A novel child-services price index links task prices to fertility decisions. Quantitative simulations calibrated to the U.S. economy suggest automation can either depress or sustain fertility depending on substitution elasticities and reskilling dynamics.

title: Scope of Research in the Domain of 3D Cadaster in the Indian Context

detail.title: Scope of Research in the Domain of 3D Cadaster in the Indian Context
detail.abstract: The study presents a context-specific, bottom-to-top exploratory approach using secondary sources to qualitatively investigate the need and scope of the 3D cadaster system in the Indian context. Starting with the literature review, the paper presents an overview of the development of 3D Cadaster literature from the past three decades to identify the research gap. Two significant research gaps are observed; the first is the lack of literature investigating the 3D cadaster's need for a 2D cadaster system in India, and the second is the lack of a systematic methodology to present a broader overview of the scope of 3D cadaster in the land administration and management domain. The paper formulates a methodology that involves identifying four Key Policy Indicators (KPIs), considering land tenure, land use, land value, and land development, respectively. The consecutive section presents the biographic overview of the land administration and management system in India, highlighting four major KPIs to define the scope of the 3D cadaster. The results and discussion provide an argument for the scope of 3D cadaster with the help of four KPIs: rising application of fractional ownership platforms (FOPs), application of land value capture (LVC) methods, promotion of mixed-use development through Transit Oriented Development (TOD) policy, and use of Transferable Development Rights (TDR) as a compensation tool. The outcome of the study indicates the need for 3D Cadaster literature to bridge the gap between the policies and practices in the domain of land administration and management in India.

title: Essay on the Topic: Digitalization and Development of Cashless Payments in the Banking System of Uzbekistan

detail.title: Essay on the Topic: Digitalization and Development of Cashless Payments in the Banking System of Uzbekistan
detail.abstract: The article analyzes the current state of non-cash payments in Uzbekistan: growth drivers, key barriers and associated risks. The role of the national digital strategy and payment infrastructure is described, as well as practical measures are proposedimproving digital literacy, expanding access in the regions, integrating banks and fintechs, and strengthening cybersecurity and consumer protection measures.

title: When Cheap Talk Has Bite
