detail.abstract: Enterprise AI adoption is not a technology decision, it is an operating model transformation. This paper presents a structured executive framework for navigating the full spectrum of Enterprise AI adoption, from traditional machine learning through autonomous, self-modifying agents. Central to the framework is a six-step decision process that forces executives to define measurable business outcomes before selecting tools, classify use cases by AI mode (Predict, Generate, Act), and select a maturity target across six levels of autonomy. A core argument of the paper is that most enterprise failures are not technical, they are organizational: unclear ownership, absent executive air cover, underfunded talent, and premature graduation to agentic systems without the foundational control infrastructure in place. The paper details the required ecosystem across both a delivery plane and a governance plane, addresses vendor lock-in strategy, demystifies the AI cost model, and provides an honest assessment of the transformation timeline most large organizations actually face. Practical roadmap guidance and a complete executive toolkit are included.

title: Multi-objective Optimization of Train Service Design in Suburban Rail with Composite Strategies
affiliations: Tongji University, Fuyang Normal University, Tongji University and Tongji University

detail.title: Multi-objective Optimization of Train Service Design in Suburban Rail with Composite Strategies
detail.abstract: To address the issue of unbalanced passenger flow in suburban rail systems, a bi-objective optimization model for train service planning is developed, integrating express/local operations, short-turning, and cross-line operational strategies. The model aims to simultaneously minimize operator costs and passenger travel time within a two-route network. A Two-Stage Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II with Hybrid Initialization (HI-TS-NSGA-II) is proposed as the solution approach. In the first stage, a heuristic algorithm is applied to minimize the number of train services under given demand and capacity constraints; in the second stage, an enhanced NSGA-II incorporating an embedded repair mechanism is utilized. Computational experiments based on the Guangzhou suburban rail system show that HI-TS-NSGA-II significantly improves computational efficiency and reduces the number of iterations required for solving the model. Analytical results further reveal that passenger travel time is approximately 1.5 times more sensitive to variations in passenger flow than operator costs. Under the Composite Operation Mode (COM), increasing the Proportion of Express Trains (PET) from 37.0% to 41.6% leads to a 29.3% increase in operator costs while reducing passenger travel time by 17.3%. Although the Proportion of Short-turning Trains (PST) exhibits inverse correlations within individual trend lines, a PST of 9% is identified as the Pareto-optimal solution across multiple scenarios. System-level analysis confirms the superiority of COM, achieving a reduction of over 6.8% in total social cost and over 7.6% in Average Travel Time of Passengers (ATTP) compared to alternative operational modes.

detail.abstract: Gartner defines augmented intelligence as a human-centered partnership model of people and artificial intelligence working together to enhance cognitive performance. Despite $2.9 trillion in projected business value and organizational investment at scale, no cross-platform, behavior-anchored, governance-integrated instrument exists to measure how well a specific person performs within that partnership at the individual level. This paper addresses that gap by introducing Human-AI Collaborative Intelligence (HACI) as the measurement science discipline that operationalizes augmented intelligence at the individual level. The Human Enhancement Quotient (HEQ) is the four-dimension assessment instrument within HACI, measuring Cognitive Agility Speed (CAS), Ethical Alignment Index (EAI), Collaborative Intelligence Quotient (CIQ), and Adaptive Growth Rate (AGR). The Augmented Intelligence Score (AIS) is the standardized composite output, defined as the arithmetic mean of the four dimensions produced through a minimum three-platform multi-AI administration protocol. Preliminary cross-platform consistency coefficient (ICC) of 0.96 was demonstrated across five independent AI architectures. Preliminary cross-user testing (n=10) suggests dimensional variance within four points and consistent identification of CIQ as the lowest-scoring dimension, aligning with independent research on human over-reliance on AI. A 2026 validation agenda targets formal psychometric validation across n=100 or more participants. Released for scholarly review and collaboration. No commercial use without written permission.

title: The National Data Trust (NDT): A Sovereign Institutional Framework for Governing the Global Data Economy
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The National Data Trust (NDT): A Sovereign Institutional Framework for Governing the Global Data Economy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This work was developed independently and reflects the author’s original research and conceptual framework.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, personal data collection, or experimental research requiring ethical approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was developed independently by the author.

detail.abstract:
Data has become the most strategic resource of the 21st century. However, despite the rapid expansion of the global data economy, most nations lack sovereign institutional frameworks capable of governing how data is accessed, exchanged, and economically utilized.

This paper introduces the concept of the National Data Trust (NDT), a sovereign institutional model designed to govern the national data economy. Functionally analogous to a central bank for data, the NDT establishes governance frameworks, regulatory standards, and trusted infrastructure for secure data exchange while enabling the creation of regulated data markets.

The paper outlines the institutional architecture, technical framework, economic model, and implementation strategy required to establish an NDT at the national level. It further explores the potential for a global network of interoperable National Data Trusts, enabling secure cross-border data exchange while preserving national sovereignty.

The NDT framework offers a structured approach for nations to reclaim digital sovereignty, unlock economic value from data, and participate in the global data economy under transparent and balanced governance conditions.

detail.abstract:
Enterprise software organizations maintain deep investments in proprietary and third-party component libraries (Angular Material, Material UI, Ant Design, and countless bespoke systems) that encode years of brand decisions, accessibility engineering, and interaction patterns accumulated over product lifetimes. The rapid adoption of AI-driven chat interfaces has introduced a fracture: teams must choose between their established design systems and the generic rendering layer imposed by existing generative UI frameworks. This paper introduces AbstractUI, not as a competing wire protocol, but as the missing enterprise automation bridge that sits upstream of today's rendering standards.

AbstractUI defines the Docket, a machine-readable JSON document describing component definitions, design token hierarchies, layout composition patterns, and framework-specific adapter mappings. The Docket is auto generated from existing codebases via a TypeScript Compiler API scanner, requiring zero manual annotation for Angular Material, MUI, Ant Design, Chakra UI, and other major libraries. We situate this contribution within the 2026 generative UI landscape, encompassing Google's A2UI, CopilotKit's AG-UI, Vercel's JSON-Render, OpenAI's Open-JSON-UI, and LogicStamp Context, and demonstrate that AbstractUI's primary novelty lies not in transport or rendering, both of which are adequately addressed by existing frameworks, but in the AST-driven scanner pipeline that eliminates the brownfield adoption barrier no other tool currently solves. We further ground the architecture in Xie and Xie's Software as Content paradigm [22] and recent HCI research on design semantics [23], arguing that AbstractUI constitutes the first production-oriented engineeringimplementation of the SaC theoretical model.

title: Critical Success Factors in Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) System Implementation in Pangasinan State University

detail.title: Critical Success Factors in Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) System Implementation in Pangasinan State University
detail.abstract: Effective leadership, efficient operations, and optimized resources are no longer enough for organizational success; the right software systems are also crucial. This paper examines the critical success factors (CSFs) of QuickCampus++, the educational enterprise resource planning (ERP) system used by Pangasinan State University (PSU). The study surveyed 60 randomly selected university officials using a Likert scale to rate the level of significance and probability of risk for each of the 22 identified CSFs. Results indicate that most of the CSFs have high or very high levels of significance, with Project Leader CSF ranking first. The planning and execution phases of the project life cycle had the highest probability of risk, and customization of the ERP system was identified as the top CSF with very high probability of risk. The ERP system provider was presented with the study results, and it adopted the information to improve future versions of QuickCampus++.

title: Behavioral Signals in Employment-Based Sponsorship: A Framework for Continuous Integrity Measurement

detail.title: Behavioral Signals in Employment-Based Sponsorship: A Framework for Continuous Integrity Measurement

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of Citlali Technologies, LLC, which develops the CitlaliBridge platform referenced in this paper.

detail.abstract: Employment-based immigration compliance in the United States has historically been assessed through discrete checkpoints: petition filings, adjudication outcomes, and periodic audits. Between these checkpoints, sponsorship behavior evolves in ways that existing oversight frameworks do not capture. This paper introduces a framework for continuous integrity measurement of H-1B sponsorship behavior using publicly available federal datasets from the Department of Labor and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. The framework defines integrity as the alignment between what employers claim in their filings and what observable data patterns reveal about their actual behavior. We organize measurement into five behavioral dimensions-Wage Integrity, Filing Integrity, Role Integrity, Outcome Integrity, and Program Integrityand specify six metrics for an initial implementation. Applied to 2.37 million H-1B Labor Condition Application filings across fiscal years 2022 through 2025, the framework yields four findings that illustrate its analytical utility, including evidence consistent with a counterintuitive market composition shift in wage-level filing patterns and a novel metric for templated filing behavior. The framework is designed to complement, not replace, existing legal and regulatory oversight, and to provide a foundation for continuous sponsorship integrity intelligence in both human and AI-assisted decision contexts.

title: Ai-Based Predictive Data Mining Algorithms for Student Profiling: A Comparative Analysis

detail.abstract: AI-based predictive data mining algorithms play an important role in the prediction-role of the two-faceted roles of data mining (classification as the other role). Having a rigid predictive algorithm is tantamount to a successful and nearhuman predictive decision in knowledge discovery among databases being implemented among government, commercial and educational sectors. In this paper, three (3) of the most commonly used AI-based predictive data mining algorithms, namely: instance-based (nearest neighbor), statistical (naive Bayes), and Bayesian networks were evaluated using academic admission data in order to assess which predictive algorithm is best suited for predicting an ideal collegiate course for a student based on the student's high school grades and historical admission records. This study sought also to find out which among the four predictive algorithms can be used in terms of volume of historical data and number of data attributes.

title: Modeling National Financial Cycles with Strong and Weak Cross-Sectional Dependence
affiliations: University of Gothenburg, University of Gothenburg,  and

detail.title: Modeling National Financial Cycles with Strong and Weak Cross-Sectional Dependence

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Although financial market fluctuations that move together are often interpreted as evidence of a global financial cycle, driven by macroeconomic and financial shocks, they may also result from spillover effects generated by local financial linkages and interdependencies among countries. This study is among the first to jointly test the impact of global common factors and local spatial spillover effects by integrating both mechanisms into a unified dynamic spatial panel data model. The global common factors are determined not only by means of a latent dynamic factor derived from a large panel of monthly data on financial variables, but also by means of cross-sectional averages of the dependent variable. Local spatial spillover effects are determined by means of spatial lags determined by neighboring countries through different metrics of proximity. Using quarterly data on national financial cycles in credit and equity markets in 25 countries over the period 1997-2019, along with four distance matrices and two control variables, we find that the dependence between countries in national financial cycles stems from a combination of all the proposed model elements. In addition, geographic distance appears to be the best performing representation of the local spillover effects between national credit cycles and economic distance between national equity cycles.

title: A Variance-Aware Benchmarking Workflow for Reproducible Deep Learning in Cervical Cytology: A Pilot Study on SIPaKMeD
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Variance-Aware Benchmarking Workflow for Reproducible Deep Learning in Cervical Cytology: A Pilot Study on SIPaKMeD
detail.abstract: Background and objective: Deep learning-based cervical cytology classification has been widely studied, yet benchmarking on small public datasets remains heterogeneous and often underreports run-to-run variability. On constrained medical imaging benchmarks, small apparent performance gains may reflect evaluation design as much as genuine model advantage. This creates a practical problem for early-stage model selection: point estimates alone may overstate ranking certainty when uncertainty reporting and development-confirmation separation are limited.Methods: To address this issue, we implemented a variance-aware, test-isolated benchmarking workflow for reproducible early-stage evaluation in cervical cytology. As a pilot study, we applied this workflow to a ResNet-50 baseline and two lightweight dual-pooling channel-attention variants on the SIPaKMeD dataset. The workflow used a fixed image-level 70/15/15 train/validation/test split, merged the training and validation subsets into a development set, performed 5-fold stratified cross-validation only within that development set, and repeated evaluation across three random seeds per configuration, yielding 54 total training runs across all models. Performance was summarized using mean accuracy, dispersion metrics, empirical run-level descriptive intervals, and exploratory paired sensitivity analyses.Results: Across repeated development runs, mean cross-validation accuracy ranged from 98.04% to 98.19%, with substantial overlap in empirical descriptive intervals. Within this workflow, ranking by mean performance diverged from ranking by variability, and the development-stage ordering did not remain stable at the held-out internal confirmation stage. These findings indicate that, on constrained public benchmarks, marginal apparent gains may be highly sensitive to the benchmarking workflow and should be interpreted cautiously.Conclusions: The main contribution of this study is methodological rather than architectural. Using a concrete cervical cytology benchmark, the proposed workflow makes ranking instability more visible through repeated evaluation, explicit uncertainty characterization, and development-confirmation separation. It may therefore serve as a practical early-stage benchmarking template for vetting candidate models before patient-level, slide-level, or prospective clinical validation.

title: Toward a Bad Job Economy: AI Adoption, Agency Costs, and Job Design
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong, Faculty of Business and Economics, The University of Hong Kong and The University of Hong Kong - University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Toward a Bad Job Economy: AI Adoption, Agency Costs, and Job Design

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study how AI affects compensation and job design when performance depends on workers' non-contractible effort. In a principal–agent model with limited liability, AI reduces effort costs but disproportionately lowers the cost of achieving satisfactory performance. This raises the incentive cost of sustaining high effort and can induce firms to replace high-wage, high-effort good jobs with low-wage, low-effort bad jobs, even when good jobs create more total surplus. As a result, AI can lower wages, reduce worker welfare, and even depress profits. If workers can adopt AI unilaterally, adoption occurs even when the resulting equilibrium harms both parties; when adoption requires worker cooperation, resistance is strongest where AI erodes rents embodied in good jobs. In a search-and-matching extension, endogenous outside options amplify these forces, reinforcing a bad-job economy and potentially reducing employment.

title: The Urban-Rural Gap in Local Market Access: Evidence from Grocery Demand
affiliations: , University of Bern and University of Duisburg-Essen

detail.title: The Urban-Rural Gap in Local Market Access: Evidence from Grocery Demand

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper leverages quasi-experimental variation from store openings and 1.5 billion grocery transactions to causally estimate the distance elasticity of grocery expenditures (−1.47) and the spatial extent of local consumption areas (approximately 16 minutes of car travel time). We embed these estimates in a nested CES demand framework to construct a granular index of local market access for nearly 350,000 grid cells (100×100m) across Switzerland. Urban areas enjoy nearly twice the consumption access of rural areas, with the 90th-to-10th percentile ratio nationally exceeding four. Compensating variation calculations show that low-income and elderly households would benefit disproportionately from improved local market access. Finally, we document that market access varies predominantly between locations, whereas income differs mostly within locations—the two dimensions are nearly orthogonal. This suggests that place-based retail policies and income-based transfers address fundamentally different dimensions of spatial inequality and should be regarded as complements.
